a1.say: Let's solve Circuit Breaker, using the State Machine approach.

a1.cap: Protect callers from a failing dependency. CircuitBreaker(threshold, cooldown) starts "closed". record(t, ok) reports a call result at time t: success resets to "closed" with zero failures; a failure increments the failure count and trips the breaker "open" once failures reach threshold (or immediately when "half-open"). allow(t) returns whether a call may proceed: an "open" breaker turns "half-open" once cooldown seconds have passed since it opened. getState() returns the state.

a1.cap: Closed: calls flow and failures are counted. Open: calls are rejected immediately so the dependency can recover. Half-open: after the cooldown, a trial call decides whether to close again or reopen.
Libraries like Resilience4j implement exactly these transitions around remote calls.
Let's walk through it with the calls CircuitBreaker(2, 10), record(1, false), record(2, false), getState(), allow(5), allow(12), record(12, true), getState().

a1.cap: 2 failures: the breaker trips open at time 2.
The cooldown has passed, so let a trial call through: half-open.
Time complexity is O(1) per call and extra space is O(1).
